propositions.text: The claimant and his family, Mexican citizens, claim refugee protection in Canada under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1).
propositions.quote: The claimant, XXXXX XXXX XXXXX, his spouse, XXXXX XXXX XXXXX XXXXX, their son, XXXXX XXXX XXXXX, and their daughter, XXXXX XXXX XXXXX XXXXX, citizens of Mexico, are claiming refugee protection in Canada under section 96 and subsection 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).

paragraphs.summary: The claimant and family, Mexican citizens, claim refugee protection in Canada under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1).

propositions.text: The principal claimant confirmed he would act as designated representative for his minor daughter during the hearing.
propositions.quote: the principal claimant, XXXXX XXXX XXXXX, confirmed during his hearing that he would assume the role of designated representative for his minor daughter, XXXXX XXXX XXXXX XXXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The principal claimant confirmed he would act as designated representative for his minor daughter during the hearing.

propositions.text: The panel is satisfied as to the claimants' identities based on their passports.
propositions.quote: the panel is satisfied as to their identities.

paragraphs.summary: The panel is satisfied as to the claimants' identities based on their passports.

propositions.text: The principal claimant alleged facts summarized in the following paragraphs.
propositions.quote: The principal claimant alleged the following.

paragraphs.summary: The principal claimant alleged facts summarized in the following paragraphs.

propositions.text: In 2008, two Mara Salvatrucha members broke into the family home, threatened and confined the claimant and family.
propositions.quote: On XXXX, 2008, two men, members of the Mara Salvatrucha, broke into the family home and threatened and forcibly confined the claimant and his family.

paragraphs.summary: In 2008, two Mara Salvatrucha members broke into the family home, threatened and confined the claimant and family.

propositions.text: In 2008, the claimant escaped the family home and took refuge at his uncle's home in Tlaxcala.
propositions.quote: On XXXX, 2008, he managed to escape the family home and take refuge at his uncle's home in Tlaxcala.

paragraphs.summary: In 2008, the claimant escaped the family home and took refuge at his uncle's home in Tlaxcala.

propositions.text: The claimant did not file a police complaint fearing Mara Salvatrucha infiltration and neighbours' killing after reporting them.
propositions.quote: He did not file a complaint with the police because he feared the Mara Salvatrucha had infiltrated the Mexican police and because the next door neighbours (XXXX XXXX) had been killed by the Mara Salvatrucha after they filed a police report against them.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant did not file a police complaint fearing Mara Salvatrucha infiltration and neighbours' killing after reporting them.

propositions.text: In 2008, the claimant left Mexico to travel to Canada and claim refugee protection.
propositions.quote: On XXXX, 2008, he left Mexico to travel to Canada and claim refugee protection.

paragraphs.summary: In 2008, the claimant left Mexico to travel to Canada and claim refugee protection.

propositions.text: In 2008, the claimant's wife and children joined him in Canada to claim refugee protection.
propositions.quote: On XXXX, 2008, the principal claimant was joined by his wife and children in Canada to claim refugee protection.

paragraphs.summary: In 2008, the claimant's wife and children joined him in Canada to claim refugee protection.

propositions.text: The claimant failed to prove a serious possibility of persecution if returned to Mexico; family claims also rejected.
propositions.quote: the panel determines that the claimant failed to discharge his burden of establishing a "serious possibility of persecution" should he return to Mexico. The claims for refugee protection filed by his wife, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, their son, XXXX XXXX XXXX, and their daughter, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX are also rejected, as they are based on the same facts as the claim filed by the principal claimant

propositions.text: The claimant and family also failed to prove on balance of probabilities that they are persons in need of protection.
propositions.quote: The panel determines that the principal claimant, his wife, and their children also failed to establish that, on a balance of probabilities, they are "persons in need of protection."

paragraphs.summary: The claimant failed to prove a serious possibility of persecution if returned to Mexico; family claims also rejected; no proof of need for protection.

propositions.text: No evidence established a nexus between claimant's fear and a Convention ground; section 96 IRPA does not apply.
propositions.quote: The panel is of the opinion that no evidence was produced by the claimant to establish a nexus between his fear and one of the five Convention grounds; therefore section 96 of the IRPA does not apply.

paragraphs.summary: No evidence established a nexus between claimant's fear and a Convention ground; section 96 IRPA does not apply.

propositions.text: Claimant's evidence did not implicate Mexican state or agents as persecutors; claim cannot proceed under IRPA 97(1)(a).
propositions.quote: The claimant's evidence did not implicate the Mexican state or one of its agents as an agent of persecution. As a result, the panel concludes that the claim cannot be considered under paragraph 97(1)(a) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant's evidence did not implicate Mexican state or agents as persecutors; claim cannot proceed under IRPA 97(1)(a).

propositions.text: Claim cannot be allowed under IRPA 97(1)(b) for reasons explained below.
propositions.quote: The panel is of the opinion that the claimant's claim for refugee protection also cannot be allowed under paragraph 97(1)(b) of the IRPA, for the following reasons.

paragraphs.summary: Claim cannot be allowed under IRPA 97(1)(b) for reasons explained below.

propositions.text: Claimant and family were victims of generalized crime and could seek refuge elsewhere in Mexico without threat.
propositions.quote: the panel concludes that the principal claimant and the members of his family were victims of generalized crime and that they could take refuge elsewhere in Mexico without being threatened or attacked by their alleged assailants.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant and family were victims of generalized crime and could seek refuge elsewhere in Mexico without threat.

propositions.text: Claimant's testimony was credible but showed assailants targeted the home, not him personally.
propositions.quote: although the claimant stated that he was personally targeted, the panel cannot agree with this statement...the assailants had just one intention: to take illegal possession of his home

paragraphs.summary: Claimant's testimony was credible but showed assailants targeted the home, not him personally.

propositions.text: Panel finds claimant credible but concludes family was not personally targeted, only the home was.
propositions.quote: The panel finds the principal claimant to be credible. However, the panel cannot conclude that he and his family were personally targeted by their assailants. In this case, it was not the individuals who were personally targeted, but rather the home they occupied.

paragraphs.summary: Panel finds claimant credible but concludes family was not personally targeted, only the home was.

propositions.text: It is implausible assailants would track claimant throughout Mexico; no evidence they tried to do so.
propositions.quote: The panel is of the opinion that it is implausible that criminals...would put so much effort into tracking him down throughout Mexico...the claimant also filed no complaint with the police and did not submit any evidence indicating that his assailants tried to find him or track him down

propositions.text: Assailants' goal was possession of home, not pursuit of claimant; claimant and family were victims of generalized crime.
propositions.quote: the panel is of the opinion that the claimant and his family were victims of generalized crime and that they were not personally targeted by their assailants, as previously mentioned. It was rather their house that was targeted.

paragraphs.summary: Panel finds it implausible assailants would track claimant; goal was home possession; claimant and family were victims of generalized crime.

propositions.text: Claimant could seek refuge in Yucatán or Zacatecas where Mara Salvatrucha are inactive; claimant's fears are implausible.
propositions.quote: The panel is not satisfied with this explanation...it is implausible that the members of this group (Mara Salvatrucha) would try to track down the claimant in the states of Yucatán or Zacatecas

propositions.text: Claimant failed to show why it would be unreasonable to relocate to Yucatán or Zacatecas or evidence of risk there.
propositions.quote: he did not give a reason why it would be unreasonable, as set out in the case law,3 to travel to the states of Yucatán or Zacatecas to seek refuge there. He also failed to submit actual and concrete evidence of conditions that would subject him to a risk

paragraphs.summary: Claimant could seek refuge in Yucatán or Zacatecas; fears implausible; failed to show unreasonableness or risk evidence for relocation.

propositions.text: Claimant fears assailants will find him but last threat was over two years ago; no recent threats reported.
propositions.quote: the last time he saw or was threatened by the two assailants dates back to XXXX 2008, over two years ago. Since XXXX 2008, the claimant has not heard any news of his assailants

paragraphs.summary: Claimant fears assailants will find him but last threat was over two years ago; no recent threats reported.

propositions.text: Claimant failed to prove relocating to Yucatán or Zacatecas would cause fear for life; assailants unlikely to pursue him.
propositions.quote: The panel is of the opinion that the claimant failed to establish, on a balance of probabilities, that relocating to another part of Mexico, specifically the states of Yucatán or Zacatecas, would cause him to fear for his life...It is implausible that the claimant would be of such interest to the alleged assailants that they would try to track him down in Mexico

paragraphs.summary: Claimant failed to prove relocating to Yucatán or Zacatecas would cause fear; assailants unlikely to pursue him.

propositions.text: It is not objectively unreasonable or unduly harsh to expect the claimant to relocate to Yucatán or Zacatecas.
propositions.quote: the panel concludes that it is not objectively unreasonable to believe or unduly harsh to expect that the claimant could relocate to the states of Yucatán or Zacatecas

propositions.text: The claimant would have no problem returning to Mexico and relocating except for fear of Mara Salvatrucha members.
propositions.quote: The claimant stated that he would have no problem returning to Mexico and relocating to one of these states, apart from his expressed fear of the members of this criminal organization (Mara Salvatrucha)

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes relocation to Yucatán or Zacatecas is reasonable; the claimant fears Mara Salvatrucha but otherwise would relocate.

propositions.text: The burden of proof for internal flight alternative rests on the claimant to show unreasonableness or conditions preventing relocation.
propositions.quote: the burden of proof regarding an internal flight alternative rests on the claimant. Thus, the claimant had to establish either that it would be unreasonable for him to seek refuge in another part of the country or that there were, in fact, conditions preventing him from relocating elsewhere

propositions.text: Case law confirms the claimant must demonstrate unreasonableness of seeking refuge elsewhere.
propositions.quote: It is settled law that in matters concerning internal flight alternatives the burden of proof is on the applicant: ... Therefore, the refugee claimant must demonstrate that it would be unreasonable for him or her to seek refuge in a different part of the country

propositions.text: The claimant must show on balance of probabilities risk of persecution in the internal flight alternative area.
propositions.quote: the burden is on the claimant to demonstrate why, on a balance of probabilities, he would face a risk of persecution in a part of the country where there is an internal flight alternative

paragraphs.summary: Prior authorities establish claimant bears burden to prove internal flight alternative is unreasonable or unsafe.

propositions.text: The claimant failed to meet the burden of proof regarding internal flight alternative.
propositions.quote: the panel is of the opinion that the claimant failed to discharge his burden of proof as required in the case law

propositions.text: There is an internal flight alternative for the claimant in Yucatán or Zacatecas.
propositions.quote: concludes that there is an internal flight alternative for him in the states of Yucatán or Zacatecas

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant failed burden and concludes internal flight alternative exists in Yucatán or Zacatecas.

propositions.text: The claimant and family are not Convention refugees or persons in need of protection under IRPA.
propositions.quote: the panel determines that the principal claimant, XXXX XXXX XXXX, his wife, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, their son, XXXX XXXX XXXX, and their daughter, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, are not "Convention refugees" or "persons in need of protection" under section 96 and subsection 97(1) of the IRPA

paragraphs.summary: The court determines the claimant and family are not refugees or in need of protection under IRPA.

propositions.text: The claims for refugee protection are rejected.
propositions.quote: their claims for refugee protection are rejected

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects the claims for refugee protection.
